# `needless-cast`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports nested identical casts, a cast whose operand is proven to already have
the target type, or a cast to the type its declaration or return already
declares.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Redundant casts imply a conversion that does not occur and can conceal the real
type flow.

## When it fires

It applies only with explicit or resolved type equality; uncertain inferred
types are left unchanged. A cast that is the whole initializer of a declaration
with a type annotation (`const x: T = @as(T, e)`) or the whole operand of a
`return` in a function returning `T` (`return @as(T, e)`) is redundant because
the destination already gives `e` the result type `T`. The two types must be
spelled with the same tokens; an alias such as `Len` for `u32`, and `!T` or `?T`
return types, which give `e` a different result type, are left alone.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn f(x: u32) u32 {
    return @as(u32, x);
}
```
